Each chosen interval of length B is invariant under the h and v steps, whose predecessor images partition it into [0,pN) and [pN,B); the complement consists of fixed d cells. This establishes bijection. Exactly sqM=MV vertical choices and spN=NH horizontal choices, with conservation giving the line counts. Separately choosing s of floor(MN/B) disjoint invariant bands and shifting a proper cyclic band establish the binomial and MN/g lower bounds with distinct active sets. The parity spin-sector statement follows from the published reconstruction theorem. originality.rationale: The concrete claimed advance is the explicit arbitrary-rectangular-period modular-band construction, its proved sectorwise binomial and translation-orbit multiplicity bounds, and the constructive parity-resolved spin realization. Jiang and Hou provide the conservation rule, determinant enumeration and boundary counts, while identifying strict-interior coefficient nonvanishing as outside their proof. Classical theory gives mean slope polytope and generic toric lattice-point/matching association; bare existential saturation is NOT treated as independently novel. Neither the inspected primary mathematical statements nor nearby result collections present this precise finite-size construction or its two multiplicity lower bounds. Priority risk remains for an implicit older lattice-path construction.
residual_risks: General toric-dimer lattice-point association may imply bare support (which is explicitly not asserted as priority novelty); an earlier direct rational-slope or Christoffel-word construction may implicitly duplicate the band algorithm.
The two lower bounds are not sharp in general and may follow from a stronger previously published multiplicity theorem that was not identified.
Independent literature priority and scientific audit have not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact finite-size sector-support question is explicitly left outside the 2026 triggering paper despite its determinant formula. A constructive O(MN) certificate for any prescribed physical slope, independent of coefficient evaluation, is useful for generating finite torus ground states and testing sector-resolved enumerations; two nontrivial multiplicity bounds guarantee distinct realizations and quantify at least a subfamily of sector degeneracy. The work makes a natural, general classification for all rectangular periods without proposing an arbitrary slice, and explicitly limits its conclusions to the zero-temperature nearest-neighbor model.
